title: The Perimeters of Something

mood.label: Reprieve, not relief 🌥️
mood.summary: A 44 built almost entirely on one piece of unratified good news — a bombing campaign against Iran's energy infrastructure called off overnight on the strength of a deal nobody has confirmed, signed or published — held against eight more Palestinians killed across Gaza, a second mass barrage on Kyiv in 48 hours that Ukraine had almost nothing left to intercept, 67 dead at the Ceuta frontier, thirteen killed in a sightseeing crash over the Nazca Lines and a Hungary that shut its only nuclear plant for the first time in its history because the Danube has fallen too low to cool it: a held breath, not an exhale.

style.genre: post-punk / darkwave — a driving RolandTR909 kit with VCSL stick-toms on a 3-of-8 euclid and a far-off woodblock, a finger-picked GM electric bass pushing straight eighths on the roots, a clipped muted electric guitar holding a two-note ostinato, a GM muted trumpet carrying the grey-bright A harmonic minor topline so the raised G# leading tone keeps straining toward a resolution the day never delivers, VCSL handbells landing sparse and wide overhead for the reprieve that hasn't touched down, a sawtooth pad breathing on a 16-cycle filter and a sine sub beneath — a deliberate turn away from the mallet / sax / harp / piano / clean-guitar palette of the last week, and a full fifth up from yesterday's D

lines: He called the bombers back in a post just after midnight —
no seal on it, no signature, no answer from the other side.
They'd agreed the perimeters of something: a shape with nothing in it,
and the alerts stayed up in ten countries while the rest of us decide.
So don't let the breath out yet — it's a reprieve, it isn't relief;
the good news is still in the air above the strait, it hasn't touched down.
Forty-four says the grey got brighter, it doesn't say the grey has gone,
and nothing that got settled overnight got settled by anyone.
Twenty-seven came at Kyiv and the sky brought exactly one of them down;
there are no interceptors left — that's the arithmetic, that's the sum.
The Danube fell past every record it had, so Hungary pulled the plug on Paks:
half a country's light gone out for want of water cold enough to run.
Somewhere a park strung six checkpoints through three hundred kilometres of forest
to keep a fever off the gorillas and the towns.
Somewhere a rover found a valley cracked in honeycombs —
old water, drying, on a world that once held on.
